# Approvals and credits

Mini-Me always **asks before** doing two kinds of things:

1. **Running a program on your computer** (for example, a small script that makes a chart).
2. **Spending credits** on a paid service.

This keeps you in control. Nothing happens until you say yes.

## "Run this on your machine?"

When Mini-Me wants to run something on your computer, the conversation pauses and a box
appears with the title **RUN THIS ON YOUR MACHINE?**. It shows exactly what will be run.

![Approving a command](images/approvals-run-command.png)

You can choose:

| Button | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Approve** | Run this one thing. Ask me again next time. |
| **Reject** | Don't run it. Mini-Me will try another way or tell you it can't continue. |
| **Approve the rest of this turn** | Run this and anything else needed **for this question only**. |
| **Approve everything in this conversation** | Don't ask again **in this conversation** (until you close the app). |

::: {.callout-tip}
If you don't read code, that's fine. The commands are normally analysis steps such as reading
your file or drawing a chart. Choosing **Approve the rest of this turn** is a good balance
between safety and not being asked too often.
:::

If you chose *Approve everything*, the bottom bar shows **approving everything — click to
stop**. Click it to go back to being asked each time.

You can turn these questions off completely in **Settings → Backend → Ask before every
command**, but we recommend leaving it on.

## AutoDiscovery and credits

**AutoDiscovery** explores a dataset on its own by running many small experiments. It uses a
paid service where **each experiment costs one credit**, so it always stops first and asks
**Start this discovery run?**

1. Read the description of what it will explore.
2. Under **EXPERIMENTS TO RUN**, choose how many experiments you want (fewer = cheaper).
3. Check how many **credits you have left**. If it says *"That is more than the credits
   left"*, choose fewer experiments.
4. Click **Run … and spend …** to start, or **Not now** to cancel.

**Nothing is spent until you press the button.**

When the run is finished, you can open it to see each experiment, its figures, and which
results **changed its beliefs the most** — the most surprising findings are marked.

## When an online service asks a question

Sometimes one of the online services Mini-Me uses needs extra information from you. A box
titled **MCP SERVICE NEEDS INPUT** appears. Fill it in and click **Send response** (or
**Continue**). Click **Decline** to say no, or **Cancel tool** to stop that step altogether.

## Switching AI company

If you change the AI company (provider) Mini-Me uses, it asks **Switch to …?** and reminds you
that questions will then be **billed to that company's account**. Click **Switch provider**
to confirm, or **Cancel** to keep the current one. Nothing is billed until you save and ask a
question.
